messages:
ciara: Quick report — our mobile app started seeing a big clump of retrying requests after devices wake from sleep. Looks like exponential backoff timers all ran at once and we got rate-limited. Anyone hit a similar Android/Kotlin SDK quirk? :facepalm:

sam: I have. Usually it's when we schedule retries with System.currentTimeMillis() + delay instead of using a monotonic clock. Do you have logs? :eyes:

ciara: Yep, pasted a tiny excerpt: 
```
2026-03-22T07:12:03Z GET /v1/generate 200
2026-03-22T07:12:53Z RETRY start id=abc123 delay=5000
2026-03-22T07:20:00Z device asleep
2026-03-22T07:45:01Z device awake
2026-03-22T07:45:01Z RETRY triggered id=abc123
2026-03-22T07:45:01Z RETRY triggered id=def456
2026-03-22T07:45:01Z RETRY triggered id=ghi789
```

ciara: All three retries that were due earlier fired at the same second after wake. SDK uses Handler.postDelayed in a background service for backoff scheduling.

elaine: Handler.postDelayed ties to wall clock time. On Android doze / time changes that can confuse it. Use SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() + delay and Handler.postAtTime or AlarmManager with ELAPSED_REALTIME_WAKEUP.

ivan: Also watch for process death / job re-creation — if you persist absolute deadlines with currentTimeMillis they'll be wrong after a timezone change or NTP update. We had a bug where restart re-applied the delay incorrectly.

sam: Repro steps I use: put device to deep sleep (~doze), schedule 3 retries with exponential backoff (5000, 15000, 45000 ms), then wake. If you used wall-clock based deadlines they all evaluate as due and run immediately.

ciara: Good call. We were serializing the nextRetryAt as epoch millis to SharedPreferences. Quick patch: store remaining backoff and compute schedule with elapsedRealtime on restore. Example snippet I threw together: 
```
// save
prefs.putLong("next_retry_monotonic", SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() + backoffMs)

// restore
val remaining = prefs.getLong("next_retry_monotonic", 0L) - SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()
val delay = max(0, remaining)
handler.postDelayed(runnable, delay)
```

elaine: That looks right. Another option is WorkManager with setBackoffCriteria(BACKOFF_POLICY_EXPONENTIAL, backoffMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) — it handles system restarts more robustly, but note it can batch multiple jobs when the system wants, so you still need jitter.

ivan: Also ensure your jitter calculation isn't lost. I saw our jitter seed defaulted to 0 on cold start, so everyone ended up with identical offsets and retries clumped. Tiny bug but nasty in production.

ciara: OMG that matches — our jitter was seeded with System.currentTimeMillis() % 1000 during init. If the process restarts after a long sleep the modulo yields the same seed across devices. Changing to SecureRandom or ThreadLocalRandom fixed variety.

sam: TL;DR fixes: use elapsedRealtime for scheduling, persist monotonic deadlines or remaining delay (not absolute wall time), use a non-deterministic jitter source, and prefer WorkManager for persisted retries. Also double-check okhttp dispatcher.maxRequests and per-host limits to avoid throttling burst.

ciara: Thanks — I'll roll a patch to persist nextRetryMonotonic + switch jitter source. Will also add a tiny integration test that simulates time jumps.

deploy-bot: deploy-start ciara/retry-fix-227 — running smoke tests

elaine: If you want I can add a small note to the SDK docs about "do not serialize wall-clock deadlines" and a code snippet showing the elapsedRealtime pattern. That helped a couple of customers. :+1:

ciara: Please do. Saving us from a 3am pager :)

ivan: One more gotcha: Retrofit CallAdapter futures that wrap a Runnable may get canceled by lifecycle observers; double-check cancellation paths — you don't want canceled requests to re-enqueue without a guard.

ciara: Will audit that. Thanks all!
